nodes.name: EurIPSpaperGPUprofiling.md
nodes.summary: Reconstructs the profiling-driven optimization methodology of a TensorNet GPU paper, from its eager-mode A100 baseline and PyTorch Profiler measurements through Triton kernel fusion and end-to-end validation. It also identifies missing microarchitectural evidence and proposes a more rigorous profiling workflow.
nodes.languageNotes: The Markdown combines quantitative profiler interpretation, CUDA kernel taxonomy, equations, and Python profiling examples.

nodes.name: cuteDSLvsTriton.md
nodes.summary: Compares Triton and NVIDIA CuTe DSL across vendor, generation, source, and performance portability, using code examples and migration scenarios to expose their different hardware-abstraction levels. It recommends Triton for irregular TensorNet2 message passing and CuTe DSL for dense, NVIDIA-specific tensor-core bottlenecks.
nodes.languageNotes: The document mixes conceptual comparison tables with paired kernel sketches and hardware-generation migration examples.

nodes.name: nsightComputeVSpytorchProfiler.md
nodes.summary: Explains how PyTorch Profiler locates globally important fusion candidates while Nsight Compute diagnoses kernel-level limits such as bandwidth, latency, occupancy, register pressure, and tensor-core utilization. It turns those signals into an escalation path spanning existing operators, torch.compile, Triton, and CuTe DSL.
nodes.languageNotes: The guide uses performance equations, symptom-to-remedy mappings, decision tables, and concrete fusion cases to connect profiling evidence to implementation choices.

nodes.name: tensornetVStensornet2.md
nodes.summary: Contrasts TensorNet's local equivariant rank-2 tensor message passing with TensorNet2's added latent charges, neutral-charge equilibration, charge-conditioned messages, and explicit long-range Coulomb energy. It derives GPU-kernel research targets for both architectures and highlights TensorNet2's quadratic electrostatics as the principal scaling challenge.
nodes.languageNotes: The Markdown develops architecture and performance implications together through tensor equations, algorithm sketches, and GPU bottleneck analysis.
